Introduction

The electric vehicle revolution is no longer a distant vision—it's happening right now across America. As EV adoption accelerates toward unprecedented levels in 2025, the infrastructure supporting these vehicles is expanding at a remarkable pace. From federal funding initiatives to innovative charging technologies, the landscape of sustainable transportation is transforming before our eyes. In Los Angeles, where climate concerns and clean air initiatives drive policy decisions, this transition is particularly significant. Shaffer Construction, Inc. is at the forefront of this revolution, helping property owners and businesses install the charging infrastructure they need to support the EV movement. Whether you're considering residential or commercial EV charger installation, understanding the current state of charging infrastructure is essential to making informed decisions about your property's electrical future.

The Explosive Growth of EV Charging Infrastructure Across America

The numbers tell a compelling story about America's commitment to electric vehicle adoption. According to the U.S. Department of Energy, the number of public EV charging ports in the United States has grown more than 6-fold over the past decade, from approximately 30,000 ports in 2016 to nearly 196,000 ports by January 2025. Even more dramatically, the availability of DC fast chargers has increased by more than 14 times over the same period, jumping from approximately 3,434 chargers in 2016 to tens of thousands today.

2025 represents a record-breaking year for EV charging deployment. Industry forecasts predict 16,700 new charging ports will open during 2025—more than 2.4 times the number deployed three years earlier in 2022. According to recent data from industry analysts, charge point operators added 699 new fast-charging stations in the third quarter of 2025 alone, bringing the total to 12,375 stations nationwide with 64,486 operational ports. This explosive growth demonstrates that the foundational charging network necessary for widespread EV adoption is finally becoming a reality. Shaffer Construction recognizes this momentum and has expanded our expertise in EV charger installation to help Los Angeles property owners capitalize on this growing infrastructure.

California's Leadership and Los Angeles' Expanding Charging Network

California is setting the national standard for EV charging infrastructure. The state has achieved a remarkable milestone: California now has 48% more public and shared private EV chargers than gasoline nozzles, according to official state data. Statewide, California has installed 178,549 public and shared private electric vehicle chargers—a testament to the state's commitment to sustainable transportation.

In Los Angeles specifically, residents and businesses have access to 8,081 public charging stations, with 293 of these offering free charging and 490 providing DC fast-charging capabilities. The city is experiencing continued expansion of charging infrastructure. For instance, Gravity is opening eight new fast-charging locations across Los Angeles in 2025, featuring cutting-edge 500 kW charging units that can deliver charging speeds twice as fast as Tesla Superchargers. Additionally, the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) is installing thousands of public charging stations throughout the city, while major providers like EVgo, Electrify America, and Tesla continue to expand their networks throughout the region.

The availability of this infrastructure makes Los Angeles an ideal location for EV ownership, and it underscores why now is the perfect time to invest in EV charger installation for your property. As discussed in our guide to EV charging infrastructure for Los Angeles property owners, property owners who install chargers now position themselves ahead of the curve. Shaffer Construction helps Los Angeles property owners navigate the installation process, handling everything from electrical assessments to permitting and final installation.

Federal Funding Programs and the NEVI Initiative Transform Charging Economics

One of the most significant drivers of charging infrastructure expansion is federal funding. The $5 billion National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) Formula Program, established through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, is distributing funding to states from 2022 through 2026 to strategically deploy EV charging infrastructure along designated Alternative Fuel Corridors. This program provides up to 80% of eligible project costs for qualifying charging station installations, including acquisition, installation, network connection, operation, maintenance, and long-term data sharing.

After a temporary funding freeze earlier in 2025, the Department of Transportation released new interim final guidance on August 11, 2025, streamlining the application process and expediting fund deployment. The updated guidance allows states to update their plans within 30 days and unlock funding faster, resuming many paused projects across the nation. This acceleration of federal support means more funding is becoming available for both public and private charging projects.

While the NEVI program primarily focuses on highway corridors, many states and municipalities have allocated additional state and local funds to support residential and commercial charging installations. California has been a leader in this area, offering various incentive programs to encourage property owners to install chargers. Shaffer Construction stays current with all available incentive programs and can help you identify funding opportunities that apply to your specific situation when you're planning commercial EV charger installation or residential upgrades in Los Angeles.

The Environmental and Economic Benefits Driving Adoption

The growth of EV charging infrastructure is driven by compelling environmental and economic imperatives. According to analyses conducted by the International Energy Agency (IEA), electric vehicles offer substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions compared to gasoline-powered vehicles. On average across the U.S., driving an electric vehicle powered by the current electricity grid produces emissions equivalent to a gasoline-powered vehicle that achieves 91 miles per gallon—and that efficiency improves every year as the grid incorporates more renewable energy sources.

Beyond environmental benefits, the economic case for EV adoption is equally strong. Electric vehicle owners enjoy significantly lower operating costs compared to traditional gasoline vehicles, including substantially reduced fuel expenses, lower maintenance requirements, and reduced brake wear due to regenerative braking systems. For commercial fleet operators and businesses seeking to reduce operational costs while improving their environmental footprint, EV charging infrastructure represents a sound investment.

The broader adoption of electric vehicles also drives technological advancement and creates new market opportunities. In Los Angeles, where environmental consciousness influences both consumer decisions and commercial strategies, businesses that embrace EV charging infrastructure demonstrate environmental responsibility while positioning themselves for long-term market relevance. Shaffer Construction understands that property owners investing in charging infrastructure today are making a forward-thinking decision that benefits both their bottom line and the environment. Technical Requirements and Professional Installation Standards

Installing EV charging infrastructure requires careful attention to electrical codes and safety standards. According to the National Electrical Code (NEC), EV charging systems fall under Article 625, which establishes specific requirements for charging equipment installation. Residential Level 2 charging stations, which operate at 240 volts, typically require a dedicated 40-ampere circuit and may necessitate an upgrade to the main electrical service panel—similar in scope to installing a new electric dryer or oven.

Commercial installations are more complex, requiring electrical distribution equipment that can support multiple charging stations simultaneously. The NEC specifies a calculated load of 7.2 kVA for each EV charging space, with load management systems necessary when multiple chargers operate simultaneously. Building codes adopted in California and Los Angeles also mandate specific charging readiness standards: new single-family dwellings with attached garages must have electrical conduits installed to support future Level 2 charging, while multifamily housing must have charging infrastructure capable of supporting chargers in 40% of parking spaces, with 10% of spaces equipped with active Level 2 chargers.

These technical requirements underscore why professional installation matters. Improper installation can lead to safety hazards, code violations, and expensive remediation. The Future of EV Charging: Innovation and Accessibility

The future of EV charging infrastructure continues to evolve with technological innovation. Industry projections indicate that the global EV charging station market will surge from approximately $28.47 billion in 2025 to $76.31 billion by 2032, growing at a compound annual growth rate of 15.1%. This expansion reflects both increasing EV adoption and continuous technological improvements in charging speed, efficiency, and accessibility.

Emerging innovations include ultra-fast charging technology capable of adding 200 miles of range in just five minutes, wireless charging systems that eliminate the need for physical connectors, and smart charging networks that optimize charging based on grid demand and electricity pricing. Battery technology continues to improve, with longer ranges and faster charging becoming standard features on new vehicles. As these technologies mature and become more widely available, the charging experience will become increasingly convenient for EV owners.

For Los Angeles property owners, this evolution presents both opportunities and challenges. Properties that invest in charging infrastructure now establish themselves as forward-thinking, environmentally responsible locations. Whether you're a commercial property manager, a multifamily housing developer, or a residential homeowner, the strategic installation of EV charging infrastructure enhances property value while supporting the region's sustainable transportation goals. As explained in our article on preparing Los Angeles buildings for the EV charging boom, property owners who act now avoid the complexity and expense of retrofitting later.

With nearly 200,000 public charging ports nationwide, $5 billion in federal NEVI funding accelerating deployment, and California leading the nation with 178,549 installed chargers, the infrastructure foundation for mass EV adoption is solidifying. In Los Angeles, where climate concerns drive policy decisions and property owners increasingly seek sustainable solutions, this transition presents both opportunity and necessity.
